evidence: Inspection ran entirely through read-only Git against the two frozen trees (base 0096a16715e1f4ece9949070ed2612b486f85ed1, candidate 1f78dd2ba136c35e7d27a9954377e631894bd604). Subcommands actually run: 'diff --name-status --no-renames', 'diff --numstat', 'diff --text --no-ext-diff --diff-algorithm=myers --no-indent-heuristic -- engine/skills/actuals_instrumentation_contract_test.go', and 'cat-file -p <tree>:<path>' against both trees. The live working tree, the index and HEAD were never read.
Manifest confirmed as a single modified entry, engine/skills/actuals_instrumentation_contract_test.go, +472/-41; no other path differs between the two trees.

Group-name comparison: TestActualsInstrumentationContract has exactly 10 t.Run groups on both sides, in identical order and with byte-identical names -- R004_R005_schema_temporal_boundary_and_interruption, R015_R006_R007_R008_checkpoint_count_description, R009_calibration_excludes_calendar_time, R010_R011_delivery_window_formula_shape, R006_R007_R015_inception_round_trip_and_explicit_zero, R014_amendedR007_fixture_pins, R001_R002_three_units_never_blended, R012_actuals_output_separate_labels, R013_roadmap_maker_no_compute_time_source_invariant, D2_D5_closed_schema_invariant. The five new t.Run groups all live under the new top-level TestActualsInstrumentationGateHelpers, so the cited ten-group list did not grow.

Only one hunk touches the body of TestActualsInstrumentationContract (base lines 210-234 replaced by the assertClosedRecordFlag call plus comment at candidate lines 214-221); every other group's assertions and messages are unchanged bytes.

Failure-message fidelity verified verbatim: all eight base failure strings ('schema must declare additionalProperties: the closed-record flag is absent', 'schema additionalProperties must be the boolean false, got %s: %v', '... got %s: a null flag does not close the record', 'schema additionalProperties must be false, got true: the record is no longer closed', "heading anchor %q must be '#'-prefixed markdown heading text", 'section heading %q not found - was the section renamed or removed?', 'section %s contains no line with marker %q', 'marker %q in section %s is not inside a top-level list item') are present unchanged in the candidate, with the same argument values (raw == schema.AdditionalProperties, flagErr.Cause == the original json.Unmarshal error). The only behavioural difference in the classifier is 'len(raw) == 0' replacing 'schema.AdditionalProperties == nil'; a non-nil zero-length json.RawMessage is unreachable from encoding/json decoding of the pinned schema, so the gate cannot observe the difference.

Extraction fidelity: the sentinel errors are compared with errors.Is at candidate lines 496, 498, 545, 547, 781 and 836, and the typed classifier error with errors.As at lines 366 and 641 -- no failure-message substring matching anywhere. The classification is asserted by typed value (flagErr.Classification != tt.want, line 644), not by message text. No dereference of closedRecord happens before the nil guard (lines 343-348).

Mutation testing (executed against a reconstructed copy of the frozen bytes in the session scratch area, never against the repository): reverting normaliseLineEndings to the single CRLF pass turns 'lone cr endings', 'mixed endings' and 'double_carriage_return_leaves_no_residual_cr' RED; reversing the two ReplaceAll calls turns 'crlf endings' and 'mixed endings' RED, confirming the documented pair-first ordering is genuinely pinned; decoding through a plain bool instead of *bool turns 'null flag does not close the record' RED; dropping the absent guard turns 'absent flag leaves the record unprovably closed' RED; making the two markdown cores return an empty string with a nil error instead of a sentinel turns 'missing heading is an error not an empty section' and 'marker present in no item is an error not an empty item' RED. Every new case except the ones named in the findings is load-bearing.

Determinism: the new test function touches no map iteration, no filesystem, no absolute path, no environment variable, no locale-sensitive operation and no clock; every input is a compile-time string literal or a byte-level strings.ReplaceAll of one. Table order is slice order. gofmt reports no diff on the frozen bytes and go vet is clean on the reconstructed copy; the full new test function passes.

Edge-case probing on the frozen cores found no panic and no vacuous pass: empty document, bare '\n', bare '\r', '\r\r\n', '#', '##', heading-with-no-trailing-newline, and heading-as-final-line all return either the correct body or errMarkdownSectionNotFound; sliceMarkdownListItem on an empty section, on a section whose first line is an indented continuation, and on a lone-CR-terminated section returns the right sentinel or item. The 'start--' walk in sliceMarkdownListItem terminates on 'start >= 0' before indexing, so hit==0 on a non-list line cannot panic (same as base).

No over-tightening: every new assertion runs against synthetic in-file fixtures, never against repository content, so no new assertion can fire on legitimate committed text. The two changes to the shared cores (full line-ending normalisation, '\r' added to the heading cutset) are strictly more permissive than base, so the existing ten groups cannot start failing on content they previously accepted. The pinned time-estimation skill document in the candidate tree contains zero carriage-return bytes, which confirms the candidate's own claim at line 611 that the normalisation branches are unreachable from committed content.

Honest labeling preserved: the R013_roadmap_maker_no_compute_time_source_invariant comment (candidate lines 188-192) and the D2_D5_closed_schema_invariant comment (lines 205-210) both still state the group is GREEN-by-construction and 'NOT RED coverage'; the new function's doc comment at lines 608-614 likewise states its own cores' branches are unreachable from committed content and that it exists so a revert cannot stay green.

Execution disclosure: the frozen file bytes were reconstructed into the session scratch area with 'cat-file -p' and compiled there as a reduced package with only TestActualsInstrumentationContract (which depends on repository-reading helpers defined in sibling files) removed; the pure cores, the classifier, and TestActualsInstrumentationGateHelpers were kept byte-identical. Nothing was executed against the repository.
